title: kv-cache-attn-seqlen-debug-scratchpad-11
body:
Context / quick summary:
- Intermittent correctness issues when switching attention kernels for long sequences (>4096) on Llama2-13B-ish weights (quantized).
- Symptoms: token-level glitches appear near sequence wrap, repeated tokens, then KV cache size drift and eventual OOM or wrong outputs.
- Repro is flaky locally but more consistent on ded-dev pool when we set seqlen=8192 and kernel=auto.

Commands run (notes + outputs):
1) baseline run (reference)
python -m run_infer --model=llama2-13b-q8 --seqlen=2048 --kernel=softmax --batch 1 --dtype=fp16 --debug-kv
-> no issues, stable KV size, generated full doc.

2) long seqlen + auto kernel (repro)
python -m run_infer --model=llama2-13b-q8 --seqlen=8192 --kernel=auto --batch 1 --dtype=bf16 --debug-kv --seed=42
LOG: selected kernel=flash_attn (runtime heuristics)
LOG: kv_cache.size=131072 (expected 131072)
...after ~17k tokens
ERROR: kv_cache: read_offset mismatch (expected 512, got 508)
TRACE: attention.cpp:248 compute_attn_kernel() -> fallback to slow_softmax
Result: repeated phrases, then model stopped producing relevant tokens.

3) force kernel to softmax for long seqlen
python -m run_infer --model=llama2-13b-q8 --seqlen=8192 --kernel=softmax --batch 1 --dtype=bf16 --debug-kv
-> produces correct output but ~2.5x slower. No kv_cache mismatch observed.

4) minimal repro (replayed prompts)
- New test harness: stress_replay.py --log-every=1 --replay-file=issue_repro.json --concurrency=2
Observed: 1/20 runs hit read_offset mismatch, always when attention kernel gets switched mid-request (kernel switching triggered by sequence length crossing 4k threshold in heuristics).

Snippets from debug logs (raw):
[2024-06-02 17:12:03.421] DEBUG kernel_selector: heuristics -> candidate=flash_attn, estimated_mem=1.8GB, estimated_speed=fast
[2024-06-02 17:12:03.422] DEBUG session: switch_kernel flash_attn -> softmax (fallback)
[2024-06-02 17:12:03.423] WARN kv_cache: write_index (1024) != read_index (1008) -- possible partial flush
[2024-06-02 17:12:03.424] ERROR kv_cache: read_offset mismatch (expected 1024, observed 1008)

Hypotheses / attempts so far:
- Hypothesis A: kernel switching path does not synchronize KV cache pointers correctly when switching from fused/packed representation (flash_attn) back to unrolled softmax. Missing memcpy or stale pointer to compacted KV layout.
  Evidence: mismatch occurs right after "switch_kernel" log line. Forcing softmax avoids the issue.

- Hypothesis B: quantized model layout (q8) uses different KV packing/alignment; flash_attn path expects 64-byte aligned blocks, fallback path expects contiguous uninterleaved layout -> the copy/transform not executed when switching because heuristics assume same layout.
  Evidence: observed only on q8/quantized builds, not on full fp16 weights.

- Hypothesis C: concurrent requests (concurrency >1) can race on shared buffer pool when kernel switch happens; pointer arithmetic uses per-thread offsets but global pool gets reallocated.
  Evidence: stress_replay with concurrency=2 increases repro rate. But we saw single-run repro too, so concurrency not necessary.

Quick notes from reading code:
- kernel_selector.cpp: select_kernel_for_sequence() returns "flash_attn" for seqlen>4096 if device has compute capability >=8.0 and mem est < threshold. Kernel switch path: session::switch_kernel() calls kernel->prepare_kv_transform(old_layout, new_layout) which should run async copy if needed.
- prepare_kv_transform() has early return if "layouts_compatible(old,new)" -> check compares stride & element_size only, not block-interleaving flag. That seems suspicious.

Reproduction plan / next steps:
1) Add more verbose dump in prepare_kv_transform to print old_layout.block_interleaved and new_layout.block_interleaved and addresses. Quick patch applied to local branch (evan/kv-switch-debug).
2) Add barrier/sync around kernel switch to ensure previous attention batch finishes and KV writes are flushed before layout transform. Sanity-check: re-run stress_replay.
3) Add unit test that constructs a packed KV buffer (flash_attn layout) then forces fallback and validates element-by-element equality after transform.
4) Try forcing retagged copy when model.is_quantized.
5) If confirms bug, hotfix: in switch path, if layouts_compatible returns true but block_interleaved differs, force transform. Add regression test.

Temporary mitigations for prod:
- Pin kernel to softmax for ded-dev pools for models with seqlen>4096 until fix ships.
- Disable heuristic switching for quantized models.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Does this affect embeddings/recall workloads that use very long prefix caching? (likely yes)
- Check whether the KV cache allocator returns the same pointer address when reusing buffers -> could mask bug in lab tests but appear in production when fragmentation occurs.
- Verify whether flash_attn fused kernel internally uses a different token ordering for past KV (I think no, but need confirmation).
- Coordinate with Maya (kernel internals) to walk through prepare_kv_transform code path.

Notes from quick experiment (results):
- With extra logging (evan/kv-switch-debug): observed old_layout.block_interleaved=true, new_layout.block_interleaved=false but layouts_compatible returned true because element_size and stride matched -> so transform skipped. That reproduces hypothesis A/B.
- Forcing transform made 10/10 repros pass (no mismatch) in harness.

Action items (who/when):
- Evan: push small PR to always compare block_interleaved flag in layouts_compatible + add logging. (PR draft in GH link above) (today)
- Maya: review kernel transform correctness and suggest efficient transform path (tomorrow)
- Owen: schedule canary to pin heuristics off for quantized models on ded-dev pool (today)
- QA: add regression case to nightly (after PR merged)

Attachments / saved artifacts:
- repro traces: /tmp/evan/kv-repro-traces-20240602.tar.gz
- local branch: evan/kv-switch-debug (WIP)

Misc brain-dump:
- Might consider adding a 'kernel_switch_dryrun' config where we validate a mock transform every N switches to catch regressions in staging without incurring cost on production.
- Consider adding pointer-tagging in debug builds so mismatched layout access throws earlier.

End of scratchpad.
